engineering_challenges.title: Charging real money for a non-deterministic, variable-cost operation
engineering_challenges.why_hard: LLM cost is unknown until the call completes, but a consumer product must quote before it charges.
engineering_challenges.resolution: Price on exactly measurable inputs (OpenAI's own input-token endpoint) plus a bounded output ceiling (input x per-feature multiplier), apply margin to that ceiling, and record actual-versus-charged per request.

engineering_challenges.title: Charge-then-generate without stealing from users
engineering_challenges.why_hard: Charging after generation gives away paid output; charging before risks taking money for a failure; concurrent requests can double-spend one balance.
engineering_challenges.resolution: Debit and OpenAI call inside one DB transaction with lockForUpdate() on the wallet row; rollback on any throwable; 422 with required_tokens before any AI call when the balance is short.

engineering_challenges.title: Structurally valid output from an LLM
engineering_challenges.why_hard: A CV is a nested object graph where prose must change but identifiers, counts and ordering must not.
engineering_challenges.resolution: strict json_schema on the API call; runtime-injected system instructions enumerating required employment IDs; safeJsonDecode() recovering from markdown fences, noise and stray terminators.

engineering_challenges.title: Payment idempotency across two fulfilment paths
engineering_challenges.why_hard: Fulfilment can be triggered by a Stripe webhook and by the browser hitting the success page; double-crediting is a direct revenue leak.
engineering_challenges.resolution: One fulfilment service guarding on event_id AND session_id against the payment_transactions ledger before crediting inside a transaction.

engineering_challenges.title: Making the economics changeable without deploys
engineering_challenges.why_hard: A pricing mistake in code requires a release; the business needed to retune prices, prompts, models and limits live.
engineering_challenges.resolution: Every lever reads from a DB table with a config fallback and tolerant try/catch; short cache on the settings singleton.

engineering_challenges.title: Operating inside an established architecture
engineering_challenges.why_hard: COPILOT_INSTRUCTIONS.md prescribes route shapes, response envelopes, validation style, migration naming and model conventions.
engineering_challenges.resolution: 35 migrations and all new endpoints follow the documented house style, with matching OpenAPI annotations.

decisions.problem: LLM cost unknown before the call
decisions.decision: Price on exact input tokens from OpenAI's input_tokens endpoint x a per-feature output multiplier, plus margin
decisions.reasoning: Gives a quotable upper bound; config/ai.php comments name the multipliers as cost/quality controls
decisions.tradeoffs: Extra network round-trip per quote; quote exceeds typical actual cost
decisions.result: Users see a firm price; actual-vs-charged recorded per request

decisions.decision: Before, inside a DB transaction with a row lock, rolled back on failure
decisions.reasoning: Code comment: 'Charge user tokens before generation'; explicit rollback message to the user
decisions.tradeoffs: Transaction held open across an external API call
decisions.result: No unpaid generation, no charge for a failure, no concurrent double-spend

decisions.problem: Pure usage pricing vs fixed prices
decisions.decision: Both: usage breakdown computed, per-feature fixed price charged (ai_feature_prices, Jan 2026)
decisions.reasoning: Fixed prices are simpler to communicate; added two months after usage pricing
decisions.tradeoffs: Margin now varies per request instead of being guaranteed
decisions.result: Predictable UX; ai_request_stats.fixed_price records charged alongside cost

decisions.problem: Where should prompts, limits and prices live?
decisions.reasoning: Migrations seed defaults; every read uses optional(...) with a config() fallback
decisions.tradeoffs: More queries; prompts become untracked state outside Git
decisions.result: Tunable in production without a deploy

decisions.problem: How to deliver AI output into the CV?
decisions.decision: Write a NEW CV/cover-letter record copying all un-optimised fields from the original
decisions.reasoning: A dense commit run on 2 Jan 2026 adds each category of persistence in turn
decisions.tradeoffs: Duplicates data; more records per user
decisions.result: The original CV is never mutated; the user compares and keeps what they want

decisions.problem: Webhook only, or also direct fulfilment?
decisions.reasoning: Code comment: 'mirrors the webhook processing to guarantee immediate fulfillment when customer is present'
decisions.tradeoffs: Two entry points to keep consistent
decisions.result: Tokens appear immediately on return from Stripe

decisions.problem: Exposing cost internals without leaking them to end users
decisions.decision: Opt-in X-AI-Debug header toggling the verbose breakdown; minimal response rebuilt when absent
decisions.reasoning: The final week of work is almost entirely this change
decisions.result: Internal tooling keeps full visibility; public responses expose only content and fixed price

decisions.problem: One very large service class, or many?
decisions.decision: Three sequential classes: OpenAiService -> Continuation -> ContinuationTwo
decisions.reasoning: Names and chronology show file growth drove the split, not domain boundaries
decisions.tradeoffs: Boundaries are historical, not conceptual; discoverability suffers

problems_solved.title: The model rewrote only the first employment
problems_solved.situation: CV optimisation sends a full employment history for rewriting.
problems_solved.problem: Valid-looking JSON returned with only the first employment rewritten; later entries unchanged or dropped; output sometimes truncated mid-JSON.
problems_solved.investigation: Evidenced by the layered countermeasures rather than a written post-mortem.
problems_solved.solution: strict json_schema; runtime-appended system instruction enumerating the employment IDs that must be returned and forbidding omissions/additions; safeJsonDecode() recovery parser.
problems_solved.result: Multi-employment optimisation became reliable enough to ship and price.

problems_solved.title: Optimisation silently discarded parts of the user's CV
problems_solved.situation: AI-optimised CVs are saved as new records.
problems_solved.problem: Only AI-returned fields were persisted, so education, skills, additional details, external activities, profile/contact fields, template and section preferences were lost.
problems_solved.solution: SaveAiResponseService extended to take the original CV and backfill every untouched field.
problems_solved.result: An optimised CV is a complete CV.
problems_solved.evidence: Nine commits on 2026-01-02; the ?array $originalCv parameter and ?? fallbacks in createCvFromAi()

problems_solved.title: Double-crediting paid top-ups
problems_solved.situation: Stripe can redeliver checkout.session.completed, and the success page also triggers fulfilment.
problems_solved.problem: Without guards one payment credits tokens multiple times — a direct revenue leak.
problems_solved.solution: Single StripeFulfillmentService checking event_id and session_id against payment_transactions before crediting; credit and ledger write in one transaction; receipt email outside it; webhook signature verification.
problems_solved.result: Fulfilment is safe to retry from any path.

problems_solved.title: Token balances could not represent real costs
problems_solved.situation: Wallet balances were unsignedInteger and Scriberly-token totals were rounded up.
problems_solved.problem: Integer-only balances forced rounding on every charge, distorting pricing and creating an unintended 'rounding profit' that had to be tracked as its own field.
problems_solved.solution: Migrations converted balance and lifetime columns to decimal with scale 2; AiTokenCalculatorService moved from ceil() to round(...,2) and zeroed rounding_profit_tokens.
problems_solved.result: Charges reflect computed cost rather than a rounding artefact.

problems_solved.title: Internal cost data leaking into public API responses
problems_solved.situation: AI responses carried model, real token usage, provider fee, margin percentage and margin tokens.
problems_solved.problem: That is the company's cost structure and margin, exposed to any authenticated user.
problems_solved.solution: X-AI-Debug header parsed by parseAiDebugHeader(); minimal response rebuilt when absent; applied across AI controllers, token calculators and the stats endpoint; header added to CORS allow-list.
problems_solved.result: One codebase serves both a safe public response and a full internal one.

implemented: Stripe webhook signature verification; missing secret fails closed
Idempotent payment fulfilment keyed on event_id and session_id
Wallet debits under lockForUpdate() inside a transaction with rollback
Sanctum bearer auth on all AI, wallet and payment endpoints; Cv/CoverLetter/User policies; explicit user_id ownership checks before reading a CV
ai_request_stats paginated per authenticated user with a hard per_page cap of 100
Cost internals suppressed unless X-AI-Debug is sent
OpenAI calls: 30s timeout, 2 retries, 200ms backoff; distinct logging for transport errors, non-2xx and JSON decode failures
Structured logging with duration_ms, http_status, response_size and token usage
Secrets in environment variables; fail-fast with a clear message when the OpenAI key is missing
weaknesses_observed: No automated tests for this subsystem; Bitbucket Pipelines entirely commented out; COPILOT_INSTRUCTIONS.md records a deliberate no-tests stance. Payment and billing logic without tests is the largest risk in this work.
Local .env sets CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGIN=* while config/cors.php reads CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS — a latent naming mismatch; production values unknown.
AiSettingsService cache TTL is 0.6 seconds, which is close to no caching.
AI generation is synchronous inside a request and a transaction rather than queued.
Prompts live in database rows, outside version control and without a review trail.

lessons: Price what you can measure: an exact input-token count plus a bounded output ceiling turns an unknowable cost into a quotable one.
Record charged-versus-actual from day one; ai_request_stats arrived in week three and made every later pricing change arguable.
Put the business levers in the database; seven weeks of commits consist of moving constants out of config and into tables.
Usage-based pricing is honest; fixed pricing is sellable. Users want a price, not a formula.
Constrain LLMs at three levels — schema, instruction and parser. Any one alone was insufficient for nested, ID-bearing JSON.
Never mutate the user's original; writing to a new record made the feature safe to iterate on and gave users a comparison view for free.
Splitting a class by line count is not refactoring; the Service -> Continuation -> ContinuationTwo chain should have been split by concern.
Ship billing with tests whatever the house policy; the absence of tests around idempotency and wallet debits is the hardest part of this work to defend.

presenting_without_metrics.principle: When you cannot show what the system did, show what the mandate was, what you built, and that it shipped.
presenting_without_metrics.why_no_metrics: Fixed-scope contract for v1; repository and database access revoked at roll-off, before the product went live. No production metric is attributable to this contributor and none should be sought.

cv_block.header: Backend / AI Engineer (Contract) — Scriberly (CV & cover-letter SaaS) · Nov 2025 – Jan 2026
cv_block.context_line: Engaged on referral to deliver the AI and payments capability for v1 of the platform; now live.
bullets: Built the platform's entire generative-AI layer — 8 AI operations on OpenAI's Responses API with strict JSON-schema outputs — and the token-credit billing system that made them sellable: per-user wallet, transactional charge-with-rollback under row-level locking, and pre-flight cost quotation so users see a firm price before any spend.

Integrated Stripe end to end (tiered Checkout top-ups, signature-verified webhooks, idempotent fulfilment across two independent paths) and a runtime pricing control plane letting the business change models, prices, margin and prompts without a deploy — 9 new tables across 35 migrations.
Delivered 35 merged pull requests in 11 weeks, plus a React 19 reference front end (sole author, 139 commits) built so the remote front-end developer could integrate the API from working code.
cv_block.why_it_works: Each bullet opens with a verb and closes with either a capability the business did not have before, or a quantity of work. Neither requires production data.

portfolio_structure: Hook: 'How do you charge a user for an AI request when you don't know what it will cost until after it finishes?'
Context: existing CV platform, startup, no in-house AI or payments capability, fixed-scope contract to build both
Constraint: firm price before the user commits; business stays margin-positive
Solution: quotation engine -> wallet -> generation -> audit chain, with the architecture diagram
Two deep dives: structured-output reliability and payment idempotency
What I'd do differently: tests for billing; decompose services by concern not file size
Honest close: delivered as v1 under contract; product went live after the engagement ended, so no production figures
presenting_without_metrics.public_writing_rule: Publish the patterns, not the project. Default to 'a UK CV-building SaaS' until explicit permission to name the client is obtained; the person to ask is the former manager who made the referral.
presenting_without_metrics.interview_script: It was a fixed-scope contract for version one, so I don't have production numbers — my access ended at delivery and the product went live afterwards. What I can tell you is what they didn't have before and what they had after: no AI integration and no payments at all, and at the end, eight AI features, a token-credit billing system, Stripe top-ups with idempotent fulfilment, and pricing the business could change without a deploy. All of it merged to master. If it's useful I can walk you through the hardest part, which was pricing an LLM call before you know what it costs.
avoid: Apologising for the absence of data or volunteering it before being asked
Inventing percentages, user counts or cost savings
Responsibility statements such as 'Worked on AI features for a CV platform'

evidence_gaps_note: Gaps 1-4, 6 and 9 cannot be closed by the contributor: access was revoked at contract end and any current production figures post-date his involvement, so they would not be attributable to him. Only gaps 5, 7, 10 and 11 are realistically worth pursuing, and only gap 5 (launch date) would change how the project is presented.
